evidence_required: connections among mathematics, lived contexts, cultures, careers, and other disciplines

units.title: Number systems, histories, and big ideas

lessons.title: Numbers across cultures: evidence and context
lessons.outcome: Investigate a culturally situated number idea, evaluate sources, and connect its development with a responsible present-day use.
prerequisites: read and compare whole numbers and fractions

practice.guided: Classify sample statements as evidence, interpretation, or unsupported claim.
practice.independent: Create a short sourced account of one number idea without treating a culture as a stereotype.
practice.retrieval: Revisit the account later and explain one mathematical and one contextual connection from memory.

lessons.title: Map the real-number family
lessons.outcome: Define and compare nested number sets, classify examples, and justify where boundary cases belong.
prerequisites: recognize common fraction and decimal forms
interpret square roots on a calculator

practice.guided: Place provided values in the smallest applicable set and explain each choice.
practice.independent: Classify a mixed set containing integers, rational values, roots, and pi-like values.
practice.retrieval: Sort new examples without the diagram and reconstruct the nesting relationship.

lessons.title: Density, infinity, and approaching a limit
lessons.outcome: Use patterns and number relationships to reason about values between values, unending sets, and quantities that approach a boundary.
representations: table and graph of an approaching sequence

practice.guided: Generate values between two given numbers and describe what the process suggests.
practice.independent: Compare an unbounded sequence with a bounded sequence that approaches a value.
practice.retrieval: Explain the difference between infinitely many terms and infinitely large values.

lessons.title: Exponent patterns and scientific notation
lessons.outcome: Use exponent patterns to explain how sign and magnitude affect a power and to express very large or small quantities efficiently.
prerequisites: understand place value and powers of ten
method_routes: place-value scaling on a number line

practice.guided: Extend positive, zero, and negative exponent patterns and check values numerically.
practice.independent: Convert contextual measurements between standard and scientific notation and evaluate powers.
practice.retrieval: Estimate the order of magnitude of unfamiliar quantities before calculating.

lessons.title: Build the exponent laws from patterns
lessons.outcome: Derive and apply relationships for multiplying, dividing, and powering powers, and explain when a rule does not apply.

practice.guided: Expand examples before generalizing the change to exponents.
practice.independent: Simplify numeric and algebraic power expressions and identify invalid shortcuts.
practice.retrieval: Choose and justify an exponent relationship in a mixed review.

lessons.title: Signed quantities in place and change
lessons.outcome: Interpret integers as locations, directions, amounts, and changes while distinguishing a position from a change in position.
representations: context table with start, change, and result

practice.guided: Translate temperature, elevation, finance, and movement statements into signed values.
practice.independent: Model multi-step changes and explain the meaning of each sign.
practice.retrieval: Distinguish negative location from negative change in new contexts.

lessons.title: Unit fractions as measures and operators
lessons.outcome: Use unit fractions to build, compare, measure, and scale fractional quantities with appropriate tools.
prerequisites: partition a whole into equal parts
method_routes: scale from one fractional part to the required amount

practice.guided: Construct non-unit fractions by repeating a selected unit fraction.
practice.independent: Solve measurement and scaling problems using unit-fraction reasoning.
practice.retrieval: Estimate and then verify a fractional measure with a different representation.

lessons.title: How signs change ratios, rates, fractions, and decimals
lessons.outcome: Explain how positive and negative signs affect equivalent forms and contextual meaning across ratios, rates, fractions, and decimals.

practice.guided: Track sign changes across equivalent numerical forms and attach a contextual meaning.
practice.independent: Compare signed rates and ratios and explain which signs describe direction or amount.
practice.retrieval: Correct common double-negative and denominator-sign errors.

lessons.title: Operate with signed fractions in formulas and measurements
lessons.outcome: Select and carry out operations with positive and negative fractions or mixed numbers in formulas, measurements, and linear contexts.

practice.guided: Choose an operation from context and maintain signs, units, and exact values.
practice.independent: Solve multi-step formula and measurement problems with signed fractions.
practice.retrieval: Estimate sign and magnitude before computing a mixed problem.

lessons.title: Rates, percentages, and proportional decisions
lessons.outcome: Pose and solve proportional problems in data, measurement, geometry, linear, and financial contexts, then check reasonableness.
prerequisites: interpret a rate per one and a percent per hundred

practice.guided: Solve the same proportional situation with two routes and compare efficiency.
practice.independent: Pose, solve, and justify a real-life proportional decision with stated units.
practice.retrieval: Select among rate, percent, and proportion methods in a mixed set.

lessons.title: Algebra across cultures and contexts
lessons.outcome: Investigate an algebraic idea in a specific cultural history and connect reliable evidence to a modern application.
prerequisites: distinguish primary and secondary source claims
method_routes: compare historical and current problem methods

practice.guided: Evaluate evidence quality in sample historical mathematics claims.
practice.independent: Produce a sourced algebra story with a demonstrated modern connection.
practice.retrieval: Explain the algebraic idea without relying on a memorized culture label.

lessons.title: Generalize patterns with expressions
lessons.outcome: Create algebraic expressions that generalize relationships shown in words, numbers, and visual patterns.
prerequisites: identify a changing and fixed quantity
method_routes: decompose a visual pattern into repeated and fixed parts

practice.guided: Translate a relationship among visual, verbal, numerical, and symbolic forms.
practice.independent: Write and test expressions for unfamiliar growing patterns and contexts.
practice.retrieval: Match expressions to patterns and explain the role of each term.

lessons.title: Prove expressions equivalent
lessons.outcome: Compare expressions using models, values, graphs, and algebra, then justify equivalence or provide a counterexample.
prerequisites: substitute a value for a variable

practice.guided: Test candidate pairs with more than one representation.
practice.independent: Prove equivalent pairs and disprove non-equivalent pairs with a valid counterexample.
practice.retrieval: Identify which property preserves equivalence in a short transformation.

lessons.title: Simplify with operation properties
lessons.outcome: Simplify algebraic expressions using valid operation properties and explain why each transformation preserves value.
prerequisites: apply distributive and associative properties numerically

practice.guided: Name the property used at each simplification step.
practice.independent: Simplify contextual expressions and verify with substitution.
practice.retrieval: Diagnose an invalid combination of unlike terms.

lessons.title: Model, solve, and verify equations
lessons.outcome: Create an equation for a context, solve it while preserving equality, and verify that the result answers the original question.
prerequisites: use inverse operations with signed numbers

practice.guided: Translate a context into an equation and justify equal changes to both sides.
practice.independent: Create, solve, and verify multi-step contextual equations.
practice.retrieval: Select an appropriate first inverse operation and explain why.

lessons.title: Variables and conditions in code
lessons.outcome: Use variables, parameters, equations, and inequalities in readable pseudocode to demonstrate algebraic relationships.
prerequisites: read a short sequence of instructions
method_routes: trace a value table by hand

practice.guided: Trace variable updates and conditional branches with supplied inputs.
practice.independent: Write bounded pseudocode that represents an equation or inequality relationship.
practice.retrieval: Predict output before running or checking the steps.

lessons.title: Decompose a mathematical process
lessons.outcome: Break a mathematical situation into ordered computational steps, identify inputs and outputs, and use the process to solve a problem.

practice.guided: Reorder and complete steps in a partially specified algorithm.
practice.independent: Design and test an algorithm for a mathematical situation with edge cases.
practice.retrieval: Explain why changing step order changes or preserves the result.

lessons.title: Predict, test, and revise code
lessons.outcome: Predict the result of readable code, test the prediction, and revise constraints or parameters for a related mathematical situation.
prerequisites: distinguish a parameter from a computed value
representations: before-and-after code diff with outcome graph

practice.guided: Predict outputs and locate the first step where an incorrect trace diverges.
practice.independent: Alter a parameter or condition and justify the new mathematical outcome.
practice.retrieval: Find and correct a small logic error without running the code first.

lessons.title: Linear and non-linear change
lessons.outcome: Compare graph shapes and rates of change, connect them with growing or shrinking patterns, and make justified predictions.

practice.guided: Match patterns, tables, and graphs and explain the rate behaviour.
practice.independent: Classify unfamiliar relations and make bounded predictions.
practice.retrieval: Distinguish constant rate from changing rate using sparse evidence.

lessons.title: Connect tables, graphs, materials, and equations
lessons.outcome: Represent a linear relation in several forms and explain how rate of change and initial value appear in each form.
prerequisites: plot points on a coordinate plane

practice.guided: Translate one relation through every representation and label corresponding features.
practice.independent: Construct missing representations from any supplied form.
practice.retrieval: Recover rate and initial value from a new table or graph.

lessons.title: Compare two linear models and interpret intersection
lessons.outcome: Compare two linear models graphically and algebraically and interpret their intersection within the limits of a context.
prerequisites: substitute a value into a linear equation

practice.guided: Connect the coordinates of an intersection with equal output values.
practice.independent: Compare contextual options and explain when each is preferable.
practice.retrieval: Estimate an intersection before solving exactly.

lessons.title: Read characteristics across representations
lessons.outcome: Compare domain, range, intercepts, rate behaviour, and other visible characteristics across graphs, tables, and equations.

practice.guided: Locate the same characteristic in three representations.
practice.independent: Compare relations and identify what each representation reveals or hides.
practice.retrieval: Infer a missing characteristic from partial information.

lessons.title: Graph equations and inequalities as points and regions
lessons.outcome: Graph selected linear and non-linear equation forms and related inequalities, then describe the points or regions that satisfy them.
prerequisites: test whether a value satisfies an equation or inequality
representations: coordinate graph with boundary or region

practice.guided: Create points for each equation form and test a point in an inequality region.
practice.independent: Graph mixed equations and inequalities and explain the solution set.
practice.retrieval: Predict graph orientation or shape from equation structure.

lessons.title: Transform lines and track equation changes
lessons.outcome: Translate, reflect, and rotate lines from a through-origin family and describe the corresponding changes in graph and equation.

practice.guided: Transform points and infer the new line before checking dynamically.
practice.independent: Describe and create transformations that meet stated conditions.
practice.retrieval: Match equation changes to transformations and justify the match.

lessons.title: Build a line equation from data
lessons.outcome: Determine a line equation from a graph, table, or concrete relation by connecting rate with slope and initial value with intercept.

practice.guided: Find the same equation from two representations and compare routes.
practice.independent: Build and use equations for unfamiliar linear situations.
practice.retrieval: Recover slope and intercept from a sparse table or graph.

lessons.title: Data at scale: value, risk, and consequence
lessons.outcome: Analyse a current large-data context and explain consequences of collection, storage, representation, and use for affected people.
prerequisites: identify a data source and variable

practice.guided: Trace sample data through its lifecycle and identify affected groups.
practice.independent: Evaluate one current context with sourced benefits, risks, and mitigations.
practice.retrieval: Explain why a technically accurate graph can still cause harm or mislead.

lessons.title: One-variable data and box plots
lessons.outcome: Represent and analyse one-variable data using appropriate summaries, quartiles, and box plots while connecting claims to the distribution.

practice.guided: Construct and annotate a box plot from an ordered data set.
practice.independent: Compare real distributions and write claims supported by centre and spread.
practice.retrieval: Estimate quartile position and detect unsupported claims from a box plot.

lessons.title: Two-variable data, regression, and prediction
lessons.outcome: Create a scatter plot, compare plausible regression models with technology, and make cautious predictions that respect correlation and range limits.

practice.guided: Describe association and compare candidate models without claiming causation.
practice.independent: Fit and evaluate a model for a real two-variable data set and bound a prediction.
practice.retrieval: Identify interpolation, extrapolation, outliers, and causal overclaiming.

lessons.title: Why mathematical models matter
lessons.outcome: Explain how mathematical models simplify situations, support decisions, and remain limited by assumptions and evidence.
prerequisites: interpret a graph or equation in context
distinguish a model from the real system

practice.guided: Identify what a sample model includes, excludes, and helps decide.
practice.independent: Critique the value and limits of a model used in a public decision.
practice.retrieval: State one useful purpose and one limitation of a remembered model.

lessons.title: Ask a modelable question
lessons.outcome: Turn an area of interest into a focused question and identify the data and contextual information needed to investigate it.
prerequisites: distinguish a broad topic from an answerable question

practice.guided: Revise broad or biased prompts into feasible model questions.
practice.independent: Propose a question with named variables, population, timeframe, and needed information.
practice.retrieval: Diagnose what information is missing from a new model question.

lessons.title: Plan and collect fit-for-purpose data
lessons.outcome: Design and carry out a safe, ethical data plan with appropriate sources, assumptions, changing factors, and controlled factors.
prerequisites: recognize basic sampling and measurement bias

practice.guided: Compare plans for validity, feasibility, privacy, and measurement consistency.
practice.independent: Carry out an approved low-risk plan or use a reviewed public data set.
practice.retrieval: Identify a hidden assumption and predict its effect on a result.

lessons.title: Build and analyse a model
lessons.outcome: Choose displays and analyses that fit the data and context, then construct a model that addresses the original question and assumptions.
prerequisites: select from one- and two-variable representations
representations: model with labelled variables and assumptions

practice.guided: Compare displays and models for the same data and justify a selection.
practice.independent: Build and test a model linked to the approved question.
practice.retrieval: Explain why an attractive display may be a poor fit for a question.

lessons.title: Report fit, limits, and predictions
lessons.outcome: Report what a model says, how well it fits, where it is limited, and which predictions are justified by the evidence.

practice.guided: Revise overconfident model claims to match the available evidence.
practice.independent: Present an answer, fit judgment, limitations, and bounded predictions for the modelling project.
practice.retrieval: Name the most consequential assumption and how it could change the conclusion.

lessons.title: Geometry and measurement across cultures and careers
lessons.outcome: Investigate a geometric idea or measurement system in a specific culture or community and connect it responsibly to careers or other disciplines.

practice.guided: Separate mathematical evidence from cultural generalization in sample accounts.
practice.independent: Create a sourced story that demonstrates the mathematics and a present connection.
practice.retrieval: Explain the mathematical relationship without reducing it to a culture label.

lessons.title: Design with lines, circles, and triangles
lessons.outcome: Create and analyse a design using valid line, circle, triangle, and angle relationships with manual or digital tools.
prerequisites: identify common triangle and circle properties

practice.guided: Complete partial constructions and justify relationships.
practice.independent: Create a design satisfying stated geometric constraints and analyse it.
practice.retrieval: Identify which relationship guarantees a required design feature.

lessons.title: Measure and convert across systems
lessons.outcome: Solve measurement problems within and between systems, including culturally or professionally situated units, with clear conversion assumptions.
representations: double number line or ratio table

practice.guided: Convert with dimensional labels and estimate before calculating.
practice.independent: Solve multi-step measurement problems and state rounding limits.
practice.retrieval: Detect and correct unit cancellation or scale errors.

lessons.title: Scale dimensions and predict measurement change
lessons.outcome: Predict and verify how changes in one or more dimensions affect perimeter, circumference, area, surface area, and volume.

practice.guided: Change one dimension at a time and record the measurement effects.
practice.independent: Solve design-change problems and justify linear, square, or cubic effects.
practice.retrieval: Predict the effect of a scale factor before using a formula.

lessons.title: Right triangles in composite designs
lessons.outcome: Use the right-triangle side relationship to solve real design and measurement problems, including composite shapes, and verify feasibility.
prerequisites: identify right triangles within a diagram

practice.guided: Identify the relevant right triangle and unknown side before calculating.
practice.independent: Solve multi-shape accessibility or construction problems with units and checks.
practice.retrieval: Determine whether the hypotenuse or a leg is unknown and estimate its size.

lessons.title: Connect prism-pyramid and cylinder-cone volume
lessons.outcome: Use and explain the volume relationships between matched prisms and pyramids and between matched cylinders and cones across units.

practice.guided: Compare matched solids and derive the one-third relationship.
practice.independent: Solve multi-unit volume and capacity problems with missing dimensions.
practice.retrieval: Choose the correct relationship from a diagram and justify it.

lessons.title: Learn from financial events and context
lessons.outcome: Analyse a past or current financial situation and use relevant mathematics and context to explain better-informed decisions without prescribing personal financial action.
prerequisites: distinguish fact, assumption, and value judgment

practice.guided: Identify mathematical and contextual factors in a sample financial event.
practice.independent: Write a sourced case analysis with more than one possible decision and stated uncertainty.
practice.retrieval: Explain how one contextual factor can change the meaning of the same calculation.

lessons.title: Appreciation and depreciation over time
lessons.outcome: Interpret and compare graphs of appreciating and depreciating values and answer questions within the supported time range.

practice.guided: Read intervals, turning points, and rates without assuming a trend continues forever.
practice.independent: Compare asset scenarios and answer evidence-bounded questions.
practice.retrieval: Distinguish value, change in value, and percent change from a graph.

lessons.title: Compare borrowing scenarios and total cost
lessons.outcome: Use appropriate tools to compare how rate, time, interest method, and down payment affect total borrowing cost, while stating assumptions and fees.
prerequisites: use powers and spreadsheets or calculators

practice.guided: Change one borrowing variable at a time and explain the total-cost effect.
practice.independent: Compare multiple disclosed scenarios without recommending a specific financial product.
practice.retrieval: Predict which variable change increases total cost and then verify.

lessons.title: Revise a budget when circumstances change
lessons.outcome: Modify a budget after a change in income, cost, priority, or timing and justify trade-offs while preserving arithmetic accuracy.

practice.guided: Repair an unbalanced budget after one stated change.
practice.independent: Create and justify two valid revisions for the same scenario.
practice.retrieval: Find an arithmetic or assumption error in a revised budget.

requirements: screen-reader-readable mathematical text and table alternatives
text descriptions for meaningful diagrams and graphs
adjustable text without loss of content or function
printable lesson, practice, and assessment packets
downloaded course operation without tutor or network
equivalent response routes that preserve the mathematical outcome
